purpose: Selumetinib is used to treat a genetic condition called neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) in children 2 years and older who have tumors called plexiform neurofibromas that cannot be completely removed by surgery. These tumors grow along nerves and can cause pain, disfigurement, or other problems. This medicine helps shrink or slow the growth of these tumors.
how_it_works: Your body has certain proteins that send signals telling cells to grow. In NF1, these signals get stuck in the 'on' position, causing tumors to grow out of control. Selumetinib blocks a specific protein called MEK that is part of this overactive signaling chain. By blocking MEK, the medicine helps slow down or stop the abnormal tumor growth.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, tiredness, rash or dry skin, mouth sores, swelling in the hands or feet, headache, fever, and muscle or joint pain. Some children may also have eye problems or heart changes, so regular check-ups are important.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems, including a decrease in how well the heart pumps. It can also cause eye problems, serious skin reactions, and liver changes. Tell your doctor right away if you notice chest pain, shortness of breath, vision changes, or severe rash. Avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen, as your skin will be more sensitive. Do not take this medicine if pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment.
typical_dosing: The dose is calculated based on the child's body surface area (height and weight) and is taken by mouth twice a day, about 12 hours apart. It should be taken on an empty stomach — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. Capsules should be swallowed whole with water and not crushed or chewed.
